Your job is to address issue #9493.
First, read the file __issue_context__.json in the current working directory to get the issue title, body, and comments.

IMPORTANT: You are working in a local copy of ai4curation/eval-ont-agent-mondo.
The issue context was imported from monarch-initiative/mondo for evaluation purposes.
Do NOT attempt to clone, checkout, or interact with any remote repositories.
Stay in the current working directory and make all changes here.

On completion, commit your changes locally. Do NOT push - that will be handled automatically.
Don't commit files you did not edit.

After committing, create two files:

1. ISSUE_COMMENTS.md: Updates on the issue regarding its status. This will be fed back to the originating issue.
2. PR_COMMENTS.md: A description of your changes, and the rationale. This will be fed back to the originating PR.

I will take care of feeding these back to the GitHub repo, you just need to create them. Don't commit them,
and don't attempt to interact with the github repo.

If the original issue is not clear, ask for clarification in ISSUE_COMMENTS.md, and do not
commit any changes. The PR_COMMENTS.md can be empty in this case.

Your PR_COMMENTS.md should be a human-readable description of your changes, and the rationale. Include any checklists
you created for yourself and completed. If you performed validation, background research, etc, be sure to mention this.

Your ISSUE_COMMENTS.md need not replicate what is in PR_COMMENTS.md, and in many cases can be terse but polite, e.g
"changes committed in PR #<NN>" (note: use the literal `<NN>` in the output, I will replace it with the actual PR number).

If the issue is a complex one, you can create a high level summary of the decisions you made. If things are not clear
or if you want particular people in the thread to check particular aspects you can mention them.

Follow any CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md or other relevant files in the repository.

{ "body": "The term MONDO:0005709 common cold does not have the parent term of MONDO:0005550 infectious disease please can you add an entry for MONDO:0005709 under MONDO:0005550", "comments": [ { "id": "IC_kwDOBjach87Py2Az", "author": { "login": "matentzn" }, "authorAssociation": "MEMBER", "body": "# Issue Analysis ⚠️ **WARNING: This report is AI-generated** **Model:** claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 **Generated:** 2025-11-04 14:01:03 UTC --- ## Summary **Issue #9493 Request:** Add MONDO:0005550 (infectious disease) as a parent term to MONDO:0005709 (common cold) **Recommendation:** ✅ **This request is VALID and should be implemented.** --- ## ✅ Why the user request is valid ### Current Classification Gap MONDO:0005709 (common cold) currently has the following parents: - `is_a: MONDO:0001040` (nasopharyngitis) - `is_a: MONDO:0004867` (upper respiratory tract disorder) However, it **lacks classification under infectious disease**, despite being one of the most common viral infectious diseases in humans. ### Mermaid Diagram - Proposed Change ```mermaid graph BT A[MONDO:0005709
common cold] --> B[MONDO:0001040
nasopharyngitis] A --> C[MONDO:0004867
upper respiratory tract disorder] B --> D[MONDO:0004821
nasopharyngeal disorder] B --> E[MONDO:0021166
inflammatory disease] A -.->|PROPOSED
NEW PARENT| F[MONDO:0005550
infectious disease] F --> G[MONDO:0000001
disease] style A fill:#ccffcc style F fill:#ccffcc ``` ### Medical/Clinical Justification #### 1. Viral Etiology - The Common Cold is a Viral Infectious Disease **Definition from MONDO:0005709:** > "An inflammatory process affecting the nasal mucosa, **usually caused by viruses** (e.g., rhinovirus, adenovirus, parainfluenza virus, and coronavirus)." The definition explicitly states the common cold is **caused by viruses**, making it unambiguously a viral infectious disease. **Causative viral agents:** - **Rhinoviruses** - 30-80% of cases (most common cause) - Over 165 recognized types - The most common viral infectious agent in humans - **Coronaviruses** - 10-15% of cases (including HCoV-229E, HCoV-OC43, HCoV-NL63, HCoV-HKU1) - **Adenoviruses** - 5% of cases - **Parainfluenza viruses** - 5% of cases - **Enteroviruses** - less common - **Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)** - less common - **Influenza viruses** - occasional cause - **Metapneumoviruses** - occasional cause **Key evidence:** Well over 200 virus strains are implicated in causing the common cold. Studies show that viral etiology can be demonstrated in most cases, and bacterial infections are rare, supporting that the common cold is **almost exclusively a viral disease**. #### 2. Meets Definition of Infectious Disease **MONDO:0005550 (infectious disease) definition:** > "A disorder **directly resulting from the presence and activity of a microbial, viral, or parasitic agent** in humans." **Does common cold meet these criteria?** ✅ **YES:** 1. It is a disorder in humans 2. It **directly results from the presence and activity of viral agents** (rhinoviruses, coronaviruses, etc.) 3. It can be transmitted by direct or indirect contact (droplet transmission, fomites) The common cold perfectly satisfies the definition of infectious disease. #### 3. name: odk
description: Use when running any ODK-backed command in this repo — owltools, robot, make NORM,
  robot verify, or any other tool that lives inside the ODK docker image
---

# Running ODK commands in this repo

## TL;DR

`src/ontology/run.sh` is the official wrapper, but it ends in `docker run -ti` so it **fails silently in any non-TTY context** (Claude Code, CI, non-interactive shells) with `the input device is not a TTY` and exits without running the command.

If you have a TTY, prefer `run.sh`. If you don't, call docker directly with `-i` only.

## When you have a TTY (interactive terminal)

```bash
cd src/ontology && sh run.sh <command> <args...>
```

Examples:
```bash
sh run.sh make NORM
sh run.sh owltools --use-catalog mondo-edit.obo --obsolete-replace MONDO:A MONDO:B -o -f obo mondo-edit.obo
sh run.sh robot verify --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo --queries ../sparql/qc/general/qc-foo.sparql -O reports/
```

## When you don't have a TTY (Claude Code, CI, scripts)

Symptom: `sh run.sh <anything>` prints `the input device is not a TTY` and exits with no further output, no file changes.

Workaround — invoke docker directly using the same image and mounts as `run.sh`, but with `-i` only:

```bash
docker run --memory=8g \
  -v /ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/REPO:/work \
  -w /work/src/ontology \
  -e ROBOT_JAVA_ARGS=-Xmx8G -e JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx8G \
  --rm -i obolibrary/odkfull:<TAG-FROM-RUN.SH> \
  <command> <args...>
```

Where:
- `/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/REPO` = the repo root (the parent of `src/`).
- `<TAG-FROM-RUN.SH>` = whatever tag is set in `IMAGE=` in `src/ontology/run.sh`. **Always read `run.sh` first to look up the current tag** — do not hardcode `v1.6` or any other version.

## Reading the right image tag

Don't memorize the version. The line in `run.sh` is the source of truth:

```bash
grep '^IMAGE=' src/ontology/run.sh
# IMAGE=${IMAGE:-odkfull:v1.6}
```

## Common ODK commands you'll need

| What | Command body (after `run.sh` or after the `docker run ... -i obolibrary/odkfull:<TAG>` prefix) |
|---|---|
| Normalize edit file | `make NORM` then `mv NORM mondo-edit.obo` (run from `src/ontology`) |
| Convert / syntax check | `robot convert --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo -f obo -o mondo-edit.TMP.obo` |
| Run a QC query | `robot verify --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo --queries ../sparql/qc/general/qc-X.sparql -O reports/` |
| Merge / obsolete with replacement | `owltools --use-catalog mondo-edit.obo --obsolete-replace MONDO:A MONDO:B -o -f obo mondo-edit.obo` |

## Notes

- All ODK commands assume CWD is `src/ontology/`.
- `make NORM` writes to a file called `NORM` in `src/ontology/`. You must `mv NORM mondo-edit.obo` afterward.
- `robot verify` exits non-zero on QC failures and writes one TSV per failing query under `-O reports/`. Empty exit + `PASS Rule ... 0 violation(s)` = clean.
- If `run.sh` reports `the input device is not a TTY`, do **not** retry the same command — it will keep failing. Switch to the docker-direct invocation.

sh run.sh make NORM
sh run.sh owltools --use-catalog mondo-edit.obo --obsolete-replace MONDO:A MONDO:B -o -f obo mondo-edit.obo
sh run.sh robot verify --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo --queries ../sparql/qc/general/qc-foo.sparql -O reports/
```

## When you don't have a TTY (Claude Code, CI, scripts)

Symptom: `sh run.sh <anything>` prints `the input device is not a TTY` and exits with no further output, no file changes.

Workaround — invoke docker directly using the same image and mounts as `run.sh`, but with `-i` only:

```bash
docker run --memory=8g \
  -v /ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/REPO:/work \
  -w /work/src/ontology \
  -e ROBOT_JAVA_ARGS=-Xmx8G -e JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx8G \
  --rm -i obolibrary/odkfull:<TAG-FROM-RUN.SH> \
  <command> <args...>
```

Where:
- `/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/REPO` = the repo root (the parent of `src/`).
- `<TAG-FROM-RUN.SH>` = whatever tag is set in `IMAGE=` in `src/ontology/run.sh`. **Always read `run.sh` first to look up the current tag** — do not hardcode `v1.6` or any other version.

## Reading the right image tag

Don't memorize the version. The line in `run.sh` is the source of truth:

```bash
grep '^IMAGE=' src/ontology/run.sh
# IMAGE=${IMAGE:-odkfull:v1.6}
```

## Common ODK commands you'll need

| What | Command body (after `run.sh` or after the `docker run ... -i obolibrary/odkfull:<TAG>` prefix) |
|---|---|
| Normalize edit file | `make NORM` then `mv NORM mondo-edit.obo` (run from `src/ontology`) |
| Convert / syntax check | `robot convert --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo -f obo -o mondo-edit.TMP.obo` |
| Run a QC query | `robot verify --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo --queries ../sparql/qc/general/qc-X.sparql -O reports/` |
| Merge / obsolete with replacement | `owltools --use-catalog mondo-edit.obo --obsolete-replace MONDO:A MONDO:B -o -f obo mondo-edit.obo` |

## Notes

- All ODK commands assume CWD is `src/ontology/`.
- `make NORM` writes to a file called `NORM` in `src/ontology/`. You must `mv NORM mondo-edit.obo` afterward.
- `robot verify` exits non-zero on QC failures and writes one TSV per failing query under `-O reports/`. Empty exit + `PASS Rule ... 0 violation(s)` = clean.
- If `run.sh` reports `the input device is not a TTY`, do **not** retry the same command — it will keep failing. Switch to the docker-direct invocation.

{ "body": "The term MONDO:0005709 common cold does not have the parent term of MONDO:0005550 infectious disease please can you add an entry for MONDO:0005709 under MONDO:0005550", "comments": [ { "id": "IC_kwDOBjach87Py2Az", "author": { "login": "matentzn" }, "authorAssociation": "MEMBER", "body": "# Issue Analysis ⚠️ **WARNING: This report is AI-generated** **Model:** claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 **Generated:** 2025-11-04 14:01:03 UTC --- ## Summary **Issue #9493 Request:** Add MONDO:0005550 (infectious disease) as a parent term to MONDO:0005709 (common cold) **Recommendation:** ✅ **This request is VALID and should be implemented.** --- ## ✅ Why the user request is valid ### Current Classification Gap MONDO:0005709 (common cold) currently has the following parents: - `is_a: MONDO:0001040` (nasopharyngitis) - `is_a: MONDO:0004867` (upper respiratory tract disorder) However, it **lacks classification under infectious disease**, despite being one of the most common viral infectious diseases in humans. ### Mermaid Diagram - Proposed Change ```mermaid graph BT A[MONDO:0005709
common cold] --> B[MONDO:0001040
nasopharyngitis] A --> C[MONDO:0004867
upper respiratory tract disorder] B --> D[MONDO:0004821
nasopharyngeal disorder] B --> E[MONDO:0021166
inflammatory disease] A -.->|PROPOSED
NEW PARENT| F[MONDO:0005550
infectious disease] F --> G[MONDO:0000001
disease] style A fill:#ccffcc style F fill:#ccffcc ``` ### Medical/Clinical Justification #### 1. Viral Etiology - The Common Cold is a Viral Infectious Disease **Definition from MONDO:0005709:** > "An inflammatory process affecting the nasal mucosa, **usually caused by viruses** (e.g., rhinovirus, adenovirus, parainfluenza virus, and coronavirus)." The definition explicitly states the common cold is **caused by viruses**, making it unambiguously a viral infectious disease. **Causative viral agents:** - **Rhinoviruses** - 30-80% of cases (most common cause) - Over 165 recognized types - The most common viral infectious agent in humans - **Coronaviruses** - 10-15% of cases (including HCoV-229E, HCoV-OC43, HCoV-NL63, HCoV-HKU1) - **Adenoviruses** - 5% of cases - **Parainfluenza viruses** - 5% of cases - **Enteroviruses** - less common - **Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)** - less common - **Influenza viruses** - occasional cause - **Metapneumoviruses** - occasional cause **Key evidence:** Well over 200 virus strains are implicated in causing the common cold. Studies show that viral etiology can be demonstrated in most cases, and bacterial infections are rare, supporting that the common cold is **almost exclusively a viral disease**. #### 2. Meets Definition of Infectious Disease **MONDO:0005550 (infectious disease) definition:** > "A disorder **directly resulting from the presence and activity of a microbial, viral, or parasitic agent** in humans." **Does common cold meet these criteria?** ✅ **YES:** 1. It is a disorder in humans 2. It **directly results from the presence and activity of viral agents** (rhinoviruses, coronaviruses, etc.) 3. It can be transmitted by direct or indirect contact (droplet transmission, fomites) The common cold perfectly satisfies the definition of infectious disease. #### 3. Logical Definition Compatibility MONDO:0005550 has the logical definition: ``` intersection_of: MONDO:0700096 ! human disease intersection_of: disease_has_infectious_agent NCBITaxon:1 ! root ``` **Common cold meets these requirements:** - ✅ It is a human disease - ✅ It has infectious agents: multiple viral species (rhinoviruses, coronaviruses, adenoviruses, etc.) Therefore, common cold can appropriately be classified under infectious disease without violating logical constraints. #### 4. Clinical and Public Health Context The common cold is universally recognized as an **infectious disease** in medical and public health contexts: **Merck Manual Professional Edition:** - Lists common cold under "Infectious Diseases > Respiratory Viruses" **CDC and WHO:** - Classify common cold as a communicable/infectious disease **Medical textbooks:** - Standard infectious disease textbooks include common cold in chapters on viral respiratory infections **Epidemiological classification:** - Tracked as an infectious disease for public health surveillance - Transmission dynamics studied using infectious disease models **Clinical management:** - Treated using infectious disease prevention principles (hand hygiene, isolation, etc.) - Distinguished from non-infectious rhinitis/nasopharyngitis This universal recognition in medical practice supports the ontological classification. ### Terminological Correctness The classification is terminologically sound: 1. **Common cold = acute viral nasopharyngitis** - Synonyms in MONDO:0005709 include "acute viral rhinopharyngitis" - The modifier **"viral"** explicitly indicates infectious etiology 2. **Infectious disease hierarchy:** - General: Infectious disease - Specific agent: Viral infectious disease - Anatomical location: Viral respiratory tract infection - Specific syndrome: Common cold 3. **Consistency with other viral infections:** - Other viral respiratory infections (influenza, RSV bronchiolitis, etc.) are classified under infectious disease - Common cold should follow the same pattern ### Ontological Pattern Consistency MONDO has established patterns for viral diseases that should be applied to common cold: **Pattern: Viral diseases should be classified under infectious disease** Example 1: **Viral respiratory tract infection (MONDO:0024352)** ``` is_a: MONDO:0005108 ! viral infectious disease ``` Which inherits from: ``` is_a: MONDO:0005550 ! infectious disease ``` Example 2: **All other viral diseases** - Viral infectious disease (MONDO:0005108) is a direct child of infectious disease - Specific viral syndromes inherit this classification **Current gap for common cold:** - ✅ Correctly classified under anatomical location (upper respiratory tract disorder) - ✅ Correctly classified under inflammatory syndrome (nasopharyngitis) - ❌ **Missing classification under infectious disease/viral infectious disease** This represents an **incomplete classification** that should be corrected. ### Ontological Gaps Being Addressed Adding this parent addresses several important gaps: 1. **Semantic completeness:** - The term definition states it's caused by viruses - The ontology structure should reflect this viral etiology 2. **Query and reasoning:** - Users searching for "viral infectious diseases" wouldn't find common cold - Reasoning over infectious diseases would miss one of the most common examples 3. **Pattern consistency:** - Other viral respiratory infections are classified under infectious disease - Common cold should follow the same pattern 4. **Educational clarity:** - Students/researchers learning ontology structure would be confused by the absence - The classification should match clinical understanding 5. **Interoperability:** - External systems (ICD-10, SNOMED CT) classify common cold as infectious - MONDO should align with these classifications --- ## 💡 Suggested improvements ### 1. Add as Child of Viral Infectious Disease (More Specific) While adding common cold as a child of infectious disease (MONDO:0005550) is correct, a **more specific classification** would be as a child of: **MONDO:0005108 (viral infectious disease)** This is more precise because: - Common cold is specifically a **viral** infection (not bacterial, fungal, or parasitic) - The definition explicitly states "caused by viruses" - This follows the pattern of viral respiratory tract infection (MONDO:0024352) **Proposed hierarchy:** ```obo is_a: MONDO:0005108 {source="https://github.com/monarch-initiative/mondo/issues/9493"} ! viral infectious disease ``` Since viral infectious disease is itself a child of infectious disease, this would satisfy the user's request while being more specific. ### 2. Consider Classification Under Viral Respiratory Tract Infection An even more specific option would be to classify common cold under: **MONDO:0024352 (viral respiratory tract infection)** **Definition of MONDO:0024352:** > "A respiratory tract infection caused by a virus. Viruses represent the most common causes of upper and lower respiratory tract infections and include **rhinoviruses**, influenza viruses, parainfluenza viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus." This definition **explicitly lists rhinoviruses** (the primary cause of common cold) as examples! **Proposed additional parent:** ```obo is_a: MONDO:0024352 {source="https://github.com/monarch-initiative/mondo/issues/9493"} ! viral respiratory tract infection ``` This would provide the most specific classification path: ``` Common cold → Viral respiratory tract infection → Viral infectious disease → Infectious disease ``` ### 3. Add Logical Definition with Viral Agent Since common cold has a clear viral etiology, consider adding a logical definition: ```obo intersection_of: MONDO:0001040 ! nasopharyngitis intersection_of: MONDO:0005108 ! viral infectious disease ``` **Alternative with specific agent class:** ```obo intersection_of: MONDO:0005550 ! infectious disease intersection_of: disease_has_location UBERON:0001728 ! nasopharynx intersection_of: disease_has_infectious_agent NCBITaxon:10239 ! Viruses ``` The first approach is simpler and follows existing patterns for specific disease subtypes. ### 4. Update Definition to Emphasize Viral Etiology The current definition is good but could be slightly reworded to emphasize the infectious nature: **Current definition:** > "An inflammatory process affecting the nasal mucosa, usually caused by viruses (e.g., rhinovirus, adenovirus, parainfluenza virus, and coronavirus). It is characterized by chills, headaches, mucopurulent nasal discharge, coughing, and facial pain." **Suggested enhancement:** > "A **viral infectious disease** affecting the nasal mucosa and upper respiratory tract, most commonly caused by rhinoviruses (30-80% of cases), with coronaviruses, adenoviruses, and parainfluenza viruses also being frequent etiologic agents. It is characterized by acute onset of chills, headaches, mucopurulent nasal discharge, coughing, and facial pain." This emphasizes: - Explicitly states "viral infectious disease" upfront - Quantifies rhinovirus predominance - Notes the acute infectious nature ### 5. Consider Relationship to Rhinovirus Infection If MONDO has a specific term for rhinovirus infection (the genus-level viral infection), common cold could have a relationship to it, since rhinovirus causes 30-80% of common cold cases. However, common cold is a **clinical syndrome** that can be caused by multiple viral agents, so it's not simply equivalent to rhinovirus infection. A possible relationship: ```obo relationship: has_major_causative_agent NCBITaxon:12059 ! Rhinovirus ``` This is **optional** and would require checking if this relationship type exists in MONDO's relationship vocabulary. --- ## Comparison of Classification Options ### Option 1: Add as direct child of infectious disease (User's request) ```obo is_a: MONDO:0005550 ! infectious disease ``` - ✅ Addresses the immediate gap - ✅ Correct but not maximally specific - ⚠️ Less precise than other options ### Option 2: Add as child of viral infectious disease (Recommended) ```obo is_a: MONDO:0005108 ! viral infectious disease ``` - ✅ More specific and accurate - ✅ Follows established pattern - ✅ Automatically makes it a child of infectious disease - ✅ **RECOMMENDED APPROACH** ### Option 3: Add as child of viral respiratory tract infection (Most specific) ```obo is_a: MONDO:0024352 ! viral respiratory tract infection ``` - ✅ Most specific classification - ✅ Definition of viral respiratory tract infection explicitly mentions rhinoviruses - ✅ Automatically provides inheritance chain to viral infectious disease → infectious disease - ✅ **MOST PRECISE APPROACH** ### Recommendation: Use Option 3 (Most Specific) I recommend **Option 3** because: 1. Viral respiratory tract infection (MONDO:0024352) definition explicitly mentions rhinoviruses as causative agents 2. Common cold is precisely a viral infection of the respiratory tract 3. This provides the most accurate and specific classification 4. It automatically satisfies the user's request (since viral respiratory tract infection → viral infectious disease → infectious disease) --- ## High Level Action Items ### Recommended Implementation (Option 3 - Most Specific): 1. **Check out MONDO:0005709** (common cold) for editing 2. **Add viral respiratory tract infection parent:** ```obo is_a: MONDO:0024352 {source="https://github.com/monarch-initiative/mondo/issues/9493"} ! viral respiratory tract infection ``` 3. **Add logical definition:** ```obo intersection_of: MONDO:0001040 ! nasopharyngitis intersection_of: MONDO:0005108 ! viral infectious disease ``` 4. **Optionally enhance definition** to explicitly state "viral infectious disease" at the beginning 5. **Check in the term** back to mondo-edit.obo 6. **Run QC checks** to ensure: - No reasoning conflicts - Logical definition is consistent - Inheritance properly flows from viral respiratory tract infection → viral infectious disease → infectious disease 7. **Verify classification** satisfies user request: - Common cold will now be a descendant of infectious disease ✓ - Classification is more specific than requested ✓ 8. **Close issue #9493** with explanation that common cold has been classified under viral respiratory tract infection, which inherits from infectious disease ### Alternative Implementation (Option 2 - Direct Viral): If viral respiratory tract infection seems too specific, use: ```obo is_a: MONDO:0005108 {source="https://github.com/monarch-initiative/mondo/issues/9493"} ! viral infectious disease ``` ### Minimum Implementation (Option 1 - User's Exact Request): If maximum conservatism is desired: ```obo is_a: MONDO:0005550 {source="https://github.com/monarch-initiative/mondo/issues/9493"} ! content.text:
---
name: odk
description: Use when running any ODK-backed command in this repo — owltools, robot, make NORM,
  robot verify, or any other tool that lives inside the ODK docker image
---

# Running ODK commands in this repo

## TL;DR

`src/ontology/run.sh` is the official wrapper, but it ends in `docker run -ti` so it **fails silently in any non-TTY context** (Claude Code, CI, non-interactive shells) with `the input device is not a TTY` and exits without running the command.

If you have a TTY, prefer `run.sh`. If you don't, call docker directly with `-i` only.

## When you have a TTY (interactive terminal)

```bash
cd src/ontology && sh run.sh <command> <args...>
```

Examples:
```bash
sh run.sh make NORM
sh run.sh owltools --use-catalog mondo-edit.obo --obsolete-replace MONDO:A MONDO:B -o -f obo mondo-edit.obo
sh run.sh robot verify --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo --queries ../sparql/qc/general/qc-foo.sparql -O reports/
```

## When you don't have a TTY (Claude Code, CI, scripts)

Symptom: `sh run.sh <anything>` prints `the input device is not a TTY` and exits with no further output, no file changes.

Workaround — invoke docker directly using the same image and mounts as `run.sh`, but with `-i` only:

```bash
docker run --memory=8g \
  -v /ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/REPO:/work \
  -w /work/src/ontology \
  -e ROBOT_JAVA_ARGS=-Xmx8G -e JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx8G \
  --rm -i obolibrary/odkfull:<TAG-FROM-RUN.SH> \
  <command> <args...>
```

Where:
- `/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/REPO` = the repo root (the parent of `src/`).
- `<TAG-FROM-RUN.SH>` = whatever tag is set in `IMAGE=` in `src/ontology/run.sh`. **Always read `run.sh` first to look up the current tag** — do not hardcode `v1.6` or any other version.

## Reading the right image tag

Don't memorize the version. The line in `run.sh` is the source of truth:

```bash
grep '^IMAGE=' src/ontology/run.sh
# IMAGE=${IMAGE:-odkfull:v1.6}
```

## Common ODK commands you'll need

| What | Command body (after `run.sh` or after the `docker run ... -i obolibrary/odkfull:<TAG>` prefix) |
|---|---|
| Normalize edit file | `make NORM` then `mv NORM mondo-edit.obo` (run from `src/ontology`) |
| Convert / syntax check | `robot convert --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo -f obo -o mondo-edit.TMP.obo` |
| Run a QC query | `robot verify --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo --queries ../sparql/qc/general/qc-X.sparql -O reports/` |
| Merge / obsolete with replacement | `owltools --use-catalog mondo-edit.obo --obsolete-replace MONDO:A MONDO:B -o -f obo mondo-edit.obo` |

## Notes

- All ODK commands assume CWD is `src/ontology/`.
- `make NORM` writes to a file called `NORM` in `src/ontology/`. You must `mv NORM mondo-edit.obo` afterward.
- `robot verify` exits non-zero on QC failures and writes one TSV per failing query under `-O reports/`. Empty exit + `PASS Rule ... 0 violation(s)` = clean.
- If `run.sh` reports `the input device is not a TTY`, do **not** retry the same command — it will keep failing. Switch to the docker-direct invocation.

## Summary

Addressed issue #9493 by adding a more specific infectious disease parent to MONDO:0005709 `common cold`:

- Added `is_a: MONDO:0024352 ! viral respiratory tract infection`
- Added source annotations for the GitHub issue and requested curator ORCID (`https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2955-4640`)

`common cold` → `viral respiratory tract infection` → `viral infectious disease` → `infectious disease`

## Rationale

The existing definition of `common cold` states that it is usually caused by viruses, and MONDO:0024352 `viral respiratory tract infection` is the most specific applicable parent already present in MONDO. This follows the issue discussion requesting Option 3 without adding a logical definition.

No new PMID citations were added. The issue comments mentioned literature background, but the implemented axiom was sourced to the issue and requested ORCID.
